Hi LM,

What I called typos is more accurately a set of punctuation inconsistencies. For example, an en dash "–" sometimes appears where an em dash "—" should be used, and dashes appear both with spaces, as in "word — word", and without them, as in "word—word". The treatment needs to be consistent, and I would use "word — word" throughout. As one example, the web title "Nolan Pierce – The Best and Greatest of Us" uses the en dash "–" rather than the em dash "—"; in the publication, it should read "Nolan Pierce — The Best and Greatest of Us". I would also put a period after every complete sentence, including sentences in blurbs and point lists, because those periods are missing in many places. For example: "Family: Married to Marisol Vega Navarro since 2006; the pair is raising three children." I hope that clarifies it.

Addressing your feedback point by point:

1\. The main cause of the inconsistent empty spaces at the ends of most articles is content length, rather than only the layout, font, or images. These articles were written for the web instead of magazine editorial use. Traditionally, the editorial team provides an approximate word count per page, and the layout is built with dummy text such as "Lorem Ipsum" before being balanced with images and blurbs. Once the pagination requirements have shaped the layout, the editorial team works to the dummy text's word count. With pre-written articles, however, the author or editorial team normally cuts or adds text until the word count fits.

Given our situation, I balanced the pages as well as possible using images and even text kerning. To make every ending match the "Confirmed Alien Existence Can’t Cast Doubt on Christianity' article", though, we need more text and/or additional images where possible. For "Made in the USA: The Return of Domestic Manufacturing", for instance, a large image on page 68 could cover as much of page 69 as possible. Images will reduce the white space, but exact consistency is possible only by adding enough text to meet the required word count. With that in mind, please send any additional images you think could be used to fill the remaining white space near article endings.

2\. The file you have is an optimized version, and the ads have not yet been replaced with the PSD versions you provided. Those replacements and corrections will all appear in the next version.

3\. If you mean the body font, it is the same one used on your website. I have nevertheless attached 8 alternative options for comparison, and my recommendation would be **Inter**.

4\. To make the layout easier to assess, I sent a spread version. The Flip Book will instead require the pages version to be uploaded. Its page count needs to be even, meaning divisible by 4. After we are through with the current work, I will test it at <https://heyzine.com>.

5\. Approval of the article pagination order is what I need before proceeding with the Table of Contents. If you are happy with that order, I can move ahead.

To fill the empty page 143, we need 4 ads now. You can also send 6-8 more ads as backups in case they are needed.

Many thanks!

In thickness, legibility, spacing, and modern appeal, I genuinely believe **INTER** is the better choice.
